subject.title: Telegram polling provider stuck in dead auto-restart loop — health monitor logs "restarting" but never actually restarts

question: Should the shared channel-lifecycle work explicitly cover the Telegram polling case where `running` is already false but a stale provider task still blocks restart, or should it be tracked as a distinct recovery invariant?
rationale: The visible failure matches the same lifecycle layer as existing reports, but the available evidence does not prove whether the open stop-timeout fix reaches a provider task that has exited into this particular stale state.

options.title: Extend the shared lifecycle scope
options.body: Recommended: make the shared channel restart repair cover stale task cleanup and safe recovery for both stopped and stop-timeout account states, with Telegram polling regression coverage.

options.title: Track a narrow Telegram follow-up
options.body: Keep this issue as a separate Telegram recovery case if source tracing proves polling ingress leaves task state that the shared stop-timeout repair cannot safely own.

recommendation.title: Extend the shared lifecycle scope
recommendation.body: Recommended: make the shared channel restart repair cover stale task cleanup and safe recovery for both stopped and stop-timeout account states, with Telegram polling regression coverage.
